title: Localized affine residue criterion and return to scheme quasi-finiteness
statement: Let $g:Z\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Choose affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Z$ such that $g(U)\subseteq V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and a point $s\in V$ represented by $\mathfrak p\subset R$. Put $B=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pB$, $k=B/\mathfrak m=\kappa(s)$, $C=A\otimes_R B$ and $F=C/\mathfrak mC$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Suppose that for every prime $P\subset C$ with contraction $\mathfrak m$ in $B$, the residue field $\kappa(P)=\operatorname{Frac}(C/P)$ has $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(P)=0$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Then the canonical maps give isomorphisms of $k$-algebras $F\cong C\otimes_B k\cong A\otimes_R k$ and of $k$-schemes $U_s\cong\operatorname{Spec}F$, where $U_s=U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Under these isomorphisms the primes $P/\mathfrak mC$ of $F$ correspond to the primes $P$ of $C$ over $\mathfrak m$ with residue field $\operatorname{Frac}(C/P)$. The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is of finite type over $k$, every point is closed, and its underlying space is finite and discrete. Consequently $\{u\in U:g(u)=s\}$ is finite and $g$ is quasi-finite at every such $u$ in the original schemes $Z,S$ [pqf-def-quasifinite]. No dimension, generic algebraicity, Noetherian, properness, or normality hypothesis is imposed on the base.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] to the given opens $U,V$. Thus $A$ is generated over $R$ by finitely many elements $a_1,\ldots,a_n$. Their images $a_i\otimes1$ generate $A\otimes_R k$ over $k$: every pure tensor $a\otimes\lambda$ is a polynomial in these images with coefficients in $k$, since $a$ is a polynomial in the $a_i$ over $R$; every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors. This uses the finite-generation description of [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: Tag 01T2, lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize; finite-generation calculation for the fibre algebra

proof.text:
Write $q:B\to k=B/\mathfrak m$. The tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives mutually inverse maps
$$C/\mathfrak mC\longrightarrow C\otimes_B k,\quad[c]\longmapsto c\otimes1,\qquad c\otimes q(b)\longmapsto[bc].$$
The first kills $\mathfrak mC$ because $bc\otimes1=c\otimes q(b)=0$ for $b\in\mathfrak m$; changing a lift $b$ changes $bc$ by an element of $\mathfrak mC$, so the second is well-defined. The composites fix $[c]$ and $c\otimes q(b)$. The same universal property gives mutually inverse maps
$$ (A\otimes_R B)\otimes_B k\longrightarrow A\otimes_R k,\quad(a\otimes b)\otimes\lambda\longmapsto a\otimes q(b)\lambda,\qquad a\otimes\lambda\longmapsto(a\otimes1)\otimes\lambda.$$
The balancing relations verify both maps, and the composites fix every pure tensor. These maps respect the $k$-actions and multiplication on pure tensors, hence are $k$-algebra isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 00E6, remark-fundamental-diagram, fibre ring as a localized quotient; explicit elementary universal-property identifications

proof.text: The quotient map $\pi:C\to F$ identifies primes $Q$ of $F$ with primes $P=\pi^{-1}Q$ containing $\mathfrak mC$: the inverse sends $P$ to $P/\mathfrak mC$, since $F/(P/\mathfrak mC)\cong C/P$ by $[[c]]\mapsto[c]$. A prime $P$ contains $\mathfrak mC$ exactly when its contraction to $B$ is $\mathfrak m$: one direction follows because this contraction is proper and contains the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and the other follows by extending the contracted ideal. The displayed quotient isomorphism identifies fraction fields, giving $\kappa(Q)=\operatorname{Frac}(F/Q)\cong\operatorname{Frac}(C/P)=\kappa(P)$ as extensions of $k$. Here $k$ embeds in $C/P$, because the kernel of $B\to C/P$ is exactly $\mathfrak m$. Thus the residue fields in the assertion and their $k$-structures agree.

proof.text:
For a prime $Q\subset F$, put $D=F/Q$ and $L=\operatorname{Frac}(D)$. By the preceding step $\operatorname{trdeg}_k L=0$. By [def-kun-transcendence-degree], a singleton $\{x\}$ cannot be algebraically independent; thus every $x\in L$ is a root of a nonzero polynomial over $k$. If $0
e x\in D$, choose such a polynomial of least degree, $c_0+c_1T+\cdots+c_dT^d$. Its degree is positive, and $c_0
e0$, since otherwise division by $T$ and $x
e0$ gives a polynomial of smaller degree vanishing at $x$. Its equation gives
$$x^{-1}=-c_0^{-1}(c_1+c_2x+\cdots+c_dx^{d-1})\in D.$$
Hence $D$ is a field and $Q$ is maximal. This argument applies to every prime; if $F=0$ there are no primes and the conclusion is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 00GA, lemma-finite-residue-extension-closed, intermediate-ring argument written out; applied in Morphisms Tag 01TE

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism], applied to $V$ at $s$, the natural map $B=R_{\mathfrak p}\to\mathcal O_{S,s}$ is an isomorphism, and by its clause (5) with $J=\mathfrak m$ the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to V$ of [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the composite $R\to B\to B/\mathfrak m=k$. Hence, by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra],
$$U_s=\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}k\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R k)\cong\operatorname{Spec}F,$$
with the projections induced by the tensor inclusions; the second isomorphism is induced by step 2. The map to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ corresponds to $\lambda\mapsto1\otimes\lambda$, so this is an isomorphism of $k$-schemes. Step 1 supplies a single affine cover with finite-type coordinate algebra over $k$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has just one point, its only opens are itself and the empty open; this cover proves local finite type directly from [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The quasi-compactness of $\operatorname{Spec}F$ in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] proves quasi-compactness of the structure map, again by checking those two opens. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is of finite type over $k$. Since step 4 makes every prime maximal, no two distinct primes are comparable. Its ring Krull dimension is at most zero by [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring] gives the same bound for its topological Krull dimension.

source.place: Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes; Algebra Tags 00E8 and 00KE; finite type checked directly over the one-point base

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-dim-zero-artinian] with $X=\operatorname{Spec}F$ and the field $k$. Step 5 verifies finite type and topological dimension at most zero, so the cited statement gives that its underlying space is finite and discrete and every point is closed. It includes the empty spectrum. By the fibre homeomorphism in [def-pc-scheme-fibre], applied to the restriction $g|_U:U\to V$ and $s\in V$, the first projection $U_s\to U$ identifies its underlying space with $\{u\in U:g(u)=s\}$, proving finiteness of that set.

Fix $u\in U$ with $g(u)=s$, represented by $\mathfrak q\subset A$ over $\mathfrak p\subset R$. The prime of $A\otimes_R k$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q$ exists by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection]. It is an isolated point because steps 2 and 6 identify this spectrum with the discrete space $\operatorname{Spec}F$. The finite-type map $R\to A$ of step 1 is therefore quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ by [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. The original affine opens $u\in U\subset Z$ and $V\subset S$, with $g(U)\subset V$, now witness quasi-finiteness of $g:Z\to S$ at $u$ in [pqf-def-quasifinite]. This proves the pointwise assertion in the original schemes using exactly these affine witnesses.
